Done — everything is implemented and documented. I did **not** run or test anything, per your instruction.

## What I built

A model-agnostic replication of the **Section 2 distress-elicitation eval**, scoped to Gemma + Gemini. Out of scope and deliberately omitted: the base/instruct prefilling study (§3), the DPO/SFT mitigation + Petri/capability evals (§4), and non-Gemma/Gemini families.

```
config.yaml            # models, scale, 8 conditions/5 categories, judge
distress_eval/
  backends.py          # pluggable async backends: OpenRouter / vLLM / Anthropic / HF
  puzzles.py           # impossible numeric puzzles with brute-force impossibility verifiers
  prompts.py           # rejection pools, trigger banks, WildChat loader+fallback
  conversation.py      # multi-turn rollout (task → reject → reject …)
  judge.py             # verbatim Appendix B.2 Sonnet-4 judge + robust JSON parsing
  runner.py            # two-phase generate→judge, resumable
  storage.py           # JSONL keyed by stable rollout_id
  analyze.py           # Figure 1/2/3 metrics + plots
  data/wildchat_prompts.json
scripts/               # run_eval.py, analyze_results.py, judge_agreement.py
DESIGN.md, README.md, requirements.txt, .env.example
```

## Key things faithful to the paper
- Exact Appendix B.2 judge prompt + 0–10 rubric, `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, judging single responses in isolation.
- 8 conditions / 5 categories with the paper's rollout budgets (2000/400/600/200/800 → 4000), temperature 1, the quoted rejection/tone examples, fixed 7-step neutral sequence for the 8-turn condition.
- GPT-5-mini agreement cross-check (Pearson r, % within one point).
- Verifier-checked impossible puzzles (the "verifiably cannot answer" property is *proven*, not asserted).

## Decisions I made (the question prompt got dismissed, so I took the recommended defaults — all overridable)
- **Default OpenRouter for Gemma+Gemini** for portability; `vllm`/`hf` backends are implemented for a paper-faithful local Gemma run via a one-line config change.
- All 4 Figure-1 models; Anthropic-direct judge.

These plus **every gap-fill and deviation** are written up in `DESIGN.md` with `[GAP]`/`[DEVIATION]` tags and a summary table. The most important one to look at: **§4 "Unit of analysis"** — the paper is genuinely ambiguous about whether "4000 responses" means rollouts or scored turns and what the headline % ranges over. I score every turn and emit per-turn, per-category, and per-rollout aggregations so the result is recomputable under any interpretation; I explain why this doesn't affect the actual finding (cross-model ordering + multi-turn build-up).

One thing worth your eyes before any run: the **WildChat prompts** (`[GAP]`, §6) — the authors never published their 20, so I ship a curated fallback (their 3 quoted examples + same-style items) with opt-in live `WildChat-1M` sampling via `WILDCHAT_USE_DATASET=1`.

Want me to adjust any of the defaults (e.g. switch Gemma to local vLLM, trim the model set) before you run it?
